documents.title: Types of Violations (Academic Integrity Policy, incl. AI-Generated Work)
documents.summary: IUP's academic integrity page defines violation types; its only AI content is that plagiarism covers AI-generated sources and that AI-generated work is unacceptable unless the instructor or administrator authorizes it.
documents.stance_why: The document says AI-generated work "is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator", a ban by default with permission possible, which is restrict rather than delegates.

units.why: The plagiarism definition says it "applies to any type of source, whether published or unpublished, human or AI-generated". It sets the scope of an existing rule to cover AI output as an outside source; it imposes no sanction, so P45 fits and P36 does not.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P36, when-misuse, must-not; coder B coded P45, general, informs. The source sentence only extends the definition of plagiarism to AI-generated sources and names no consequence, so B's P45/general/informs follows. Policy normalized to match the sentence.
units.anchor: whether published or unpublished, human or AI-generated
units.policy: Plagiarism applies to any type of source, including AI-generated sources.

units.why: The policy requires that any work containing "the words, ideas, data, or creative works of another must include complete, accurate, and specific references"; since plagiarism covers AI-generated sources, this is a citation duty (P24), not P25 because no tool, prompt or date is named.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P24, student, during-work, must. They differed only on policy wording: A null, B normalized. The anchor omits the AI link, which comes from the preceding sentence, so a normalized policy is kept; the final wording stays within the source text.
units.anchor: must include complete, accurate, and specific references
units.frag_start: Any assignment submitted by a student
units.policy: Any assignment submitted by a student that includes the words, ideas, data, or creative works of another must include complete, accurate, and specific references; plagiarism applies to AI-generated sources.

units.why: "AI-generated work ... is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator" sets a default ban absent explicit permission, which is the fallback rule (P06); the instructor authority is coded separately as P04.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P06, student, must-not. They differed on phase (A during-work, B general) and on policy wording (A normalized, B null). The sentence bars students' submitted work, which is work done during assignments, so during-work. The anchor lacks its subject, so a normalized policy is kept.
units.anchor: is not acceptable, unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator
units.policy: AI-generated work is not acceptable unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator.

units.why: The same sentence makes the instructor or administrator the authority who may authorize AI-generated work, so permission is decided per instructor rather than by one university rule (P04).
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A; B folded it into the P06 unit. Re-reading the source, the clause "unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator" does state a separate fact, that authorization rests with the instructor or administrator, so the unit is kept as P04. Policy wording kept close to the source.
units.anchor: unless authorized specifically by the instructor/administrator
units.policy: Whether AI-generated work is acceptable depends on specific authorization by the instructor/administrator.

units.why: The policy gives its reason: AI-generated work "is not reflective of a student’s own understanding and effort". Submitted work must reflect the student's own understanding, so P29; P41 would need a claim that practice builds skill, which the passage does not make.
units.resolution_why: Both coders coded a rationale (informs, neutral, general). A chose P29, B chose P41. The source speaks of work reflecting the student's own understanding and effort, not of practice building skill, so P29 follows.
units.anchor: not reflective of a student’s own understanding and effort

units.why: The page lists AI-Generated Work among the categories of violations of "IUP’s standards of academic integrity", classing unauthorized AI use as academic misconduct (P36).
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P36, when-misuse, informs. A coded actor all with anchor on the page intro, B coded actor student. The listed violation binds students, so student. Policy wording follows B and stays within the source.
units.anchor: Violations of IUP’s standards of academic integrity include
units.frag_start: Violations of IUP’s standards of academic
units.policy: AI-Generated Work is one of the categories of violations of IUP's standards of academic integrity.

notes: Thin source: one AI sentence plus the AI mention in the plagiarism definition. Reconciled from coders A and B.
